# Unibox

> One immutable Dart description of a screen, drawn by Flutter and rendered as HTML a crawler can read.

Unibox is a Dart 3.13 workspace of eight packages, in one direction only: the model,
then the web, then the widgets. `packages/unibox_core` holds the node tree and the design
tokens and has no dependencies at all. The web renderer is two packages, so that a second
web renderer stays possible: `packages/unibox_css` turns a token into declarations and
`packages/unibox_element` turns a node into an element plan, before anyone writes it.
`packages/unibox_html` writes that plan as a document, and `packages/unibox_dom` adopts
that document in a browser and keeps it in step with the stores the tree created.
`packages/unibox_flutter` draws the same tree as widgets. `packages/unibox_testing` holds
the tables of expected presentation that the renderer suites are checked against, so the
renderings cannot drift apart silently. `packages/unibox_material` turns the Material 3
type scale and colour roles into the same tokens and builds its components on `Box`.

Paths in this file are relative to the repository root. This is an index: the rules a
coding agent needs are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), and a human contributing needs
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the instruction set for a coding agent — non-negotiable
  rules, repository map, commands, and the touch points for a token, a node type,
  a parity fix or an example change.
- [README.md](README.md): the user guide. One section per node, with the parameter
  tables, typography, motion, semantics, serving a tree, and what the host owns.
- [design.md](design.md): why the model looks like this — defaults, precedence,
  dimensions, parity, interaction, non-goals, compatibility.

## Building an app with Unibox

- [AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md](AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md): the condensed model, a Flutter/CSS →
  Unibox translation table, a complete component, a stateful page with a dialog and
  a checklist, written to be pasted into an assistant's context by someone writing
  application code.
- [example/unibox_example_shared/lib/](example/unibox_example_shared/lib/): a complete
  application as one `StatefulNode` — navigation bar, list, form, dialog — in plain
  Dart. The arrangement to copy for a real application.

## Packages

- [unibox_core](packages/unibox_core/README.md): the model — nodes, tokens,
  defaults, validation. Pure Dart; never imports `dart:ui`, Flutter or a web framework.
- [unibox_css](packages/unibox_css/README.md): the CSS the web renders from, a token as a
  declaration, the four state rules, the `:root` theme, and the canonical text a class
  name is hashed from. Pure Dart, no dependencies.
- [unibox_element](packages/unibox_element/README.md): the element plan — what each node
  becomes, before anyone writes it — and the stylesheet that gives every look its class.
  Shared by every web renderer. Pure Dart.
- [unibox_html](packages/unibox_html/README.md): the web renderer — a tree as a
  document a search engine can read, with no framework and no runtime. Pure Dart, no
  dependencies.
- [unibox_dom](packages/unibox_dom/README.md): the client renderer — adopts the markup the
  server wrote and patches it as the stores publish, so a page is interactive without
  Flutter.
- [unibox_flutter](packages/unibox_flutter/README.md): the Flutter renderer
  (`renderFlutter`, `node.toWidget()`), node by node, with what differs from the web.
- [unibox_testing](packages/unibox_testing/README.md): the presentation contract —
  `BoxAppearance` + `boxCases`, `TextAppearance` + `textCases`, `OverlayAppearance`
  + `overlayCases` — and the line between "the same" and "close enough". Test only.
- [unibox_material](packages/unibox_material/README.md): the Material 3 type roles
  as `BoxTextStyle` values (`MaterialTypography`, `MaterialTypeRole`), the colour
  roles as `MaterialPalette` (`light`/`dark`, or grown from one seed colour with
  `fromSeed` and its `MaterialSchemeVariant`), and the components built on the nodes
  the renderers already draw — `MaterialCard`, `MaterialListTile`, `MaterialButton`,
  `MaterialChip`, `MaterialSegmentedButton`, `MaterialTabBar`, `MaterialTabs`,
  `MaterialNavigationBar`, `MaterialIcon`, `MaterialInkWell`, `MaterialTextField`,
  `MaterialDialog`, `MaterialBottomSheet` — optional and pure Dart, for a tree that wants Material on both
  targets.

## Working on the repository

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): setup, the fast loop, what "done" means for a token
  or a node, the commit convention, and what is out of scope.
- [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md): the Contributor Covenant in short, and where a
  report goes.
- [MAINTENANCE.md](MAINTENANCE.md): what runs on its own (CI, the weekly gate,
  Dependabot), the monthly hour, what a human decides, and the prompt that hands a
  maintenance task to an assistant.
- [tool/verify.sh](tool/verify.sh): format check, analysis and the test
  suites, the way CI runs them; it reads `.flutter-version` first, and stops when the
  machine's Flutter is not the one the repository is developed against. `--fast` skips the
  suites, `--docs` adds `dart doc`.
- [tool/scale.sh](tool/scale.sh): the synthetic benchmark — a page with thousands of
  nodes, planned and written — and `tool/scale_check.py`, which holds it to the
  baseline in `tool/scale_baseline.json`. Runs in CI.
- [tool/maintenance.sh](tool/maintenance.sh): the slower monthly pass — the gate with the
  docs, the performance budget, the site build and the numbers the README quotes.
- [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml), and
  [.github/workflows/weekly.yml](.github/workflows/weekly.yml) for the scheduled gate:
  what continuous integration
  actually runs, including the docs job that fails on a `dart doc` warning.
- [.github/workflows/review.yml](.github/workflows/review.yml) and
  [.github/agent/review-prompt.md](.github/agent/review-prompt.md): the second reader — every
  pull request is read against `AGENTS.md` and answered in one comment. It approves nothing.
- [tool/surface_check.py](tool/surface_check.py): every token has a place in the appearance table
  or a reason in the script's map, and every callback is reached by both renderers.
- [.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/maintenance_task.yml](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/maintenance_task.yml): the
  form that makes an issue `agent-ready` — the recipe, the package, the line that has to pass.
  [MAINTENANCE.md](MAINTENANCE.md#the-queue) says what the labels mean.
- [TASK_PLAN.md](TASK_PLAN.md): what is built, the decisions taken, and the
  `Deferred` list that is deliberately out of scope.
- [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md): the human release checklist. CI never publishes.
- [example/README.md](example/README.md): the example's trees, the two hosts, and how a
  document and a Flutter app are built from them.

## Optional

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the three-page pointer a Claude Code session reads, which forwards
  to [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) rather than repeating it.
- [analysis_options.yaml](analysis_options.yaml): the strict analyzer settings and
  the enabled lints.
- [packages/unibox_core/CHANGELOG.md](packages/unibox_core/CHANGELOG.md),
  [packages/unibox_flutter/CHANGELOG.md](packages/unibox_flutter/CHANGELOG.md),
  [packages/unibox_html/CHANGELOG.md](packages/unibox_html/CHANGELOG.md),
  [packages/unibox_dom/CHANGELOG.md](packages/unibox_dom/CHANGELOG.md): the unreleased
  changes, which is where a new token is described for the user.
- [PERFORMANCE.md](PERFORMANCE.md): what a page with thousands of nodes costs, the three
  shapes the benchmark measures, the baseline CI holds them to, and the six places the
  pipeline was not linear before they were fixed.
- [example/unibox_example_shared/lib/](example/unibox_example_shared/lib/): the
  example trees as plain Dart, the arrangement to copy for a real application.
